title: Implement cancellable stream iterator with graceful deadline fallback
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Problem: current Go SDK streaming helpers return raw proto/rd streams that are awkward to use with context cancellation and short client deadlines. Clients frequently need: 1) a simple iterator API that always respects ctx.Done(), 2) clear semantics when client deadline is shorter than server-prepared responses, and 3) resumable reconnect semantics for transient network failures without leaking server-side resources.

Goal: implement a new ergonomics-focused StreamIterator type in the Go SDK that: (a) exposes Next(ctx) / Close(ctx) semantics that are well-documented and cancel-safe, (b) performs a bounded graceful-fallback when ctx deadline triggers during an in-flight chunk (to avoid abrupt server-side orphaning), (c) supports resumable reconnects using server-provided resume tokens with configurable retry/backoff, and (d) is configurable for prefetch/backpressure and observability metrics.

Non-goals: changing server protocol, introducing new wire-level requirements, or forcing breaking API changes for existing fine-grained stream consumers. This should be additive and opt-in through a new constructor in the Go SDK.
acceptance_criteria: New StreamIterator API added under sdk/go/streaming with constructor NewStreamIterator(client, opts...)
Next(ctx) blocks until an item is available or ctx is done, returning context.Canceled or context.DeadlineExceeded appropriately
When ctx deadline elapses mid-chunk the client attempts a configurable graceful-fallback window (default 200ms) before closing the RPC to avoid orphaned server work
Resumable reconnects use server resume tokens; SDK retries transient failures up to default 3 attempts with jittered backoff
Integration tests exercising context cancellation, deadline-around-chunk, and resume-reconnect behavior are present and green on CI
Telemetry emitted: stream_open, stream_close, stream_resume_attempt, stream_resume_success, stream_error with tags for model/route
Docs and Go example added showing idiomatic Cancel + Defer Close(ctx) usage and migration notes for existing consumers
No observable performance regression for non-stream APIs (benchmarks run; delta < 5% median p99)
notes: 2025-02-18: Ticket created after customer support call where a PLG user reported context cancellation leaking GPU inference reservations.
2025-02-19: Spike implemented a small prototype showing 200ms grace window prevents server-side orphan while not worsening p99 by more than 2% on internal microbenchmarks.
2025-02-20: API proposal reviewed with SDK owners (Riley, Diego, Amara). Decided on non-breaking constructor NewStreamIterator(ctx, client, opts...) rather than replacing existing streaming helpers.
2025-02-22: UX review feedback: add explicit Close(ctx) that returns final error to help users surface server-side terminal errors. Accepted.
2025-02-24: Integration test harness added to runtime test cluster; discovered race when Close() and resumable reconnect run concurrently; fixed by introducing singleflight reconnect gate.
2025-02-25: Security reviewed resume token usage; no secrets transported beyond opaque token, reviewer (Nina Kapoor) marked security_review_required=false.

test_plan: Unit tests: fakeServer stream that yields items with configurable delay; assert Next(ctx) returns items or context errors as expected
Race tests: concurrent Close(ctx) + Next(ctx) + internal reconnect triggered to ensure no double-close or leaked goroutines
Integration: run against staging inference runtime with long-running chunks to validate grace window behavior under real latencies
Load test: iterate 1k concurrent streams for 10 minutes to ensure p99 token allocation and no resource leak
CI gating: require flake-free on linux-amd64 and linux-arm64 runners before marking Done
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag 'stream_iterator_v1' default-enabled for new minor release
Stage rollout: SDK pre-release (rc) -> canaries (internal customers) for 2 weeks -> GA
Communicate migration guide in SDK release notes and update Go examples repository
Monitor telemetry dashboards for stream_resume_attempt and stream_error spikes for 72 hours post-GA
migration_notes: Existing users of the low-level streaming API can continue to use current helpers; StreamIterator is opt-in and exposed in package streaming
For callers that used manual goroutine+channel stop patterns, recommend replacing with: for it.Next(ctx) { ... } err := it.Close(ctx)
Note: Close(ctx) surfaces final server error. If callers previously ignored final server errors, they should audit call sites before migration.
